rq: joint identification of raw-language equivalence and latent intervention-target partition
primary_work: Cross-audit consolidation of C026-C063 into a residual joint automorphism criterion and decision gate
reason: Across the audited CRL, interactive-grounding, active-probing, causal-abstraction, and language-dynamics literature, perfect recovery of internal causal or functional objects remains compatible with a non-trivial joint recoding of utterance classes, target blocks, denotation, and target-indexed world interfaces. Adaptive interaction also preserves the ambiguity when query, response, and cost laws are equivariant. Joint identification therefore requires independently fixed symmetry-breaking observations and elimination of merge/split alternatives inside complete transcript-equivalence blocks.
surviving_rq: After independently recovering the finest raw-language quotient and finest non-language intervention-target quotient, can preregistered cross-system probes whose identities, orientations, units, costs, and response laws are fixed independently of both codebooks reduce the residual joint automorphism group to the declared trivial equivalence group and eliminate merge/split alternatives, thereby identifying Q, residual P, and d without parser, simulator-label, reward, evaluator, or clarification-codebook leakage?

governance_proposition.name: Residual Joint Automorphism Criterion
governance_proposition.necessary_condition: No non-trivial admissible joint automorphism may preserve every allowed adaptive transcript and cost while changing Q, P, or d.
